players.product: regulated electric service, gas generation and transmission build for hyperscale data centers in the Gulf South (Meta Richland Parish LA, Amazon Mississippi)

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 2026 results: adjusted EPS of $0.86 with 2026 guidance affirmed; industrial sales growth was 'very strong at 15% as new and expansion projects continued to ramp up their operations' and overall retail sales increased 6%; CFO said the strong quarter does not change the full-year expectation ('way too early' to point to the high end).
quarterly_data.figure: adjusted EPS $0.86; industrial sales 15%; retail sales 6%

quarterly_data.signal: Outlooks raised on the new Meta agreement: 'approximately 8.5% compound annual retail sales growth through 2029, driven by 16% industrial growth', with data centers a significant driver alongside LNG, industrial gases, petrochemicals, agricultural chemicals and primary metals; adjusted EPS outlook for next year is $0.20 higher, rising to $0.50 higher in 2029 to $6.40; 2028-to-2029 adjusted EPS growth was 12% and roughly the same is expected for 2030 (full outlook extended to 2030 at the June Investor Day).
quarterly_data.figure: 8.5% retail sales CAGR through 2029; 16% industrial growth; 2029 adjusted EPS outlook $6.40

quarterly_data.signal: Four-year capital plan is now $57 billion, $14 billion higher than last quarter, mainly for the new customer agreement: seven new CCCTs (in-service dates in 2030 and 2031, so not all of their capital is in the four-year horizon) plus battery storage; transmission in the Meta filing, the renewables and the Riverbend nuclear upgrade are not yet included; CFO described the CCCT capital as 'largely overnight costs' with financing costs largely excluded.

Load pipeline: even after all agreements signed to date including Meta, Entergy still has 'a pipeline of 7 G-12 GW of potential data center customers that are not in our plan' (Meta moved through it and was backfilled with new interest); hyperscale data centers enter the plan only after a signed electric service agreement and at minimum bill levels, which on hyperscalers are 'significantly higher' than on traditional customers; separately, ESAs totaling over 1,000 MW were signed this year across multiple industries (steel, petrochemicals, many under 20 MW), included on a probability-weighted basis.
quarterly_data.figure: 7 GW-12 GW data center pipeline outside plan; over 1,000 MW of new non-Meta ESAs

quarterly_data.signal: Funding the build: equity associated with the four-year plan is now $6.6 billion (low end of the 10%-15% of capital target); forward agreements cover about 30% of the need, with $1.9 billion already contracted and $4.7 billion to be sourced, not expected to be needed until late 2027 through 2029; forecast also includes $3 billion of hybrid instruments at parent; FFO to debt at or above 15% on Moody's metric throughout the period.
quarterly_data.figure: $6.6 billion equity need; $1.9 billion contracted; $4.7 billion to be sourced

quarterly_data.signal: Renewables and storage: active RFPs for more than 1,600 MW of renewables and storage, and over 4,500 MW in negotiation after prior RFPs in Arkansas, Louisiana and Mississippi, roughly two-thirds of which would be owned; CFO said 'About half of that is not in our plan'. Meta (2,500 MW in the new agreement, 1,500 MW in the previous one) and other customers signed up for multi-gigawatt solar, to be filled through open RFPs and self-builds (solar or batteries).
quarterly_data.figure: more than 1,600 MW in active RFPs; over 4,500 MW in negotiation

quarterly_data.signal: Generation and grid execution: Orange County Advanced Power Station (Texas) achieved first fire and is expected fully online in late summer; Entergy Texas issued an RFP in February for combined cycle capacity and energy; power delivery identified more than $30 million in capital savings on the Commodore to Churchill 230 kV project, a design improvement applicable to future large transmission projects.
quarterly_data.figure: more than $30 million capital savings (Commodore to Churchill 230 kV)

quarterly_data.signal: New nuclear: CEO said new nuclear will be needed long term and the Meta agreement 'helps move that forward a little bit' (the agreement includes further investigating CCS, nuclear upgrades and new nuclear; asked about the AP1000 reference in the agreement's study, he said the AP1000 has been constructed and has a full design), but Entergy is 'more or less agnostic to the technology' and focused on construction risk sharing — 'Our balance sheet isn't big enough to cover the whole risk by ourselves'; asset M&A beyond Cottonwood not expected to be significant.

connects_to.relationship: regulated electric service and dedicated generation for Meta's Richland Parish, Louisiana hyperscale data center (full-tariff customer)

contracts.signal: In late March Entergy announced a new electric service agreement with Meta for another data center in North Louisiana; Entergy Louisiana filed with the Louisiana PSC for seven new combined cycle units, transmission infrastructure and battery storage, with costs covered by payments from Meta; the commission placed it under the Louisiana Lightning Initiative targeting a decision at the December B&E meeting. Entergy is 'requesting approval for more than $15 billion in capital with about $14 billion in our four-year plan' and agreed to pursue another 2.5GW of renewables and further investigate CCS, nuclear upgrades and new nuclear for Meta's clean energy goals; the fair share value of this agreement alone is expected to be $2 billion (within the $7 billion total customer benefits). CCCTs finish in 2031; full load comes as those assets come online, with minimum bills during the ramp.
contracts.units: seven new combined cycle units; 2.5GW of renewables
contracts.value: more than $15 billion in capital requested; $2 billion fair share value
contracts.type: electric service agreement (second North Louisiana data center)

contracts.signal: Under the new agreement, over the next 20 years Meta committed $140 million for energy efficiency programs and $60 million for Entergy's Power to Care program (Entergy Louisiana matching Power to Care, bringing the increase to $120 million).
contracts.value: $140 million energy efficiency; $60 million Power to Care

connects_to.relationship: electric service for AWS's data center investment in Mississippi (Entergy's first hyperscale customer)

contracts.signal: CFO: under Superpower Mississippi Entergy is 'deploying $300 million of capital without incremental cost to customers because of the embedded cost that AWS is supporting'.
